top_issues: Color-only meaning: green/violet bars encode 'yours now' vs 'promised' with no text labels, inaccessible to colorblind users and to Rosa (01-home, bar group under $155.00).
'How to read this' is a paragraph of protocol text that must be opened; the key distinction (promised could fail) is buried.
'send up to 175.00' / 'receive up to 0.50' reads as a limit, not a spending ceiling — Jamal can't tell what is instantly spendable at a glance.
fixes: Add one plain-English line above the bar: 'Green = money you can use right now. Purple = money a hub has promised that could still fail.'
Put small text labels ('yours now', 'promised') directly on the bar segments instead of relying on the legend.
Replace 'receive up to X' with a single prominent 'Instantly spendable' number on the balance card.

top_issues: '25.00 nets what H1 owes you' is confusing — the before/after bars shift and 'receive up to 0.50' stays next to the After bar.
Route strip (You/H1/H2) is clean, but fee 'under 0.01 USDC' hides the basis-point detail behind a route expander.
The 'Provable' box explains co-signatures well but is an extra read before the user can just send.
fixes: Replace '25.00 nets what H1 owes you' with 'After this payment, H1 will owe you 90.00' in plain words.
Show the fee as a concrete amount (not 'under') in the payment summary line.
Move the 'Provable' explanation into a tooltip on the Pay button so it never blocks the send action.

top_issues: 'Frame #71' and 'Verified by your runtime' are unexplained jargon for a first-time payer.
Proof hash is shown with no label about what it proves or how to use it for an audit.
Modal dims the underlying screen heavily, which is fine for focus but removes context for the 'Download/Print' comparison.
fixes: Add a one-line tooltip on Frame: 'A frame is a co-signed record of this payment.'
Label the hash 'Proof (for audits)' and add a 'What does this prove?' link.
Keep the modal but show a faint breadcrumb of the account so users know which account was debited.

top_issues: 'Prepare incoming account / H1-Testnet' — 'prepare' is protocol jargon; a first-time receiver won't know why they must choose before sharing.
'25.50 capacity via H1' and 'Capacity is checked for this account. The sender chooses the final route.' require two reads to understand.
QR is excellent for mobile but the desktop layout relegates the amount field to a small card.
fixes: Rename 'Prepare incoming account' to 'Choose where this payment lands' and default to the best option.
Replace 'capacity' language with 'This hub can accept up to 25.50 for you right now.'
Let the user generate a plain payment link without choosing an account first, with account selection as an optional advanced step.

top_issues: 'Lot rounding 0.000004 USDC stays with you' and 'basis' are trader jargon in the fee strip.
The book is excellent, but the spread line and fee strip bundle three numbers with no hierarchy.
Settlement 'bilateral — signed by both sides' is good, but 'Gross receive' vs net is a heavy paragraph.
fixes: Show one bold line: 'You receive ≈0.039992 WETH after fees' and move Gross/Lot details behind an info button.
Give the spread its own clear label with the exact cost in USDC, not just a ratio.
Reduce the 'Gross receive' block to two lines: fees, then net receive.

top_issues: Dead-end: 'Prepare incoming capacity before swapping' error halts a first-time cross-network user with no path to fix it.
Legs panel (Tron / Clear) reads as legal boilerplate and crowds the collateral controls.
Collateral 100/50/0% options plus the 'Add 10% buffer' checkbox stack too much logic before the swap is allowed.
fixes: On an empty 'Preparing incoming capacity' state, show a one-tap 'Add collateral now' that pre-fills 100% and explains why, so the flow never dead-ends.
Collapse the Legs panel into a single 'How this crosses networks' explainer.
Move the 10% buffer to a per-user default and surface it only as an advanced toggle.

top_issues: Legend has five color states (secured/promised/you owe/credit room/in flight) with tiny text — hard to parse at a glance.
The '+90.00 they owe you' headline is strong, but 'Their credit line to you / Your credit line to them' is a mentally heavy pair.
'Collateral 60.00' is green but not explained as what is enforceable on-chain.
fixes: Put text labels on the bar itself and increase the legend font size.
Rename credit lines to 'What they can send you' / 'What you can send them'.
Label Collateral as 'On-chain enforceable' next to the value.

top_issues: The modal dims and obscures the account panel it references, so the user can't see what they are disputing.
The dispute relies on a numbered 3-step read to communicate risk; no single-line risk callout exists.
'Dispute this account...' is the only actionable element and sits low under the steps.
fixes: Keep the underlying account visible and highlight the disputed lane.
Add a one-line risk summary at the top: 'If H1 stops responding, this freezes the account and moves to the chain.'
Promote the Dispute button to the top of the modal and keep the steps as a collapsible explainer.

top_issues: '2 committed entries' and 'From your runtime's committed frames' are protocol jargon in a transaction log.
The right detail panel shows Frame #71 and proof but repeats the same 'committed frames' phrasing.
Filters are good, but the 'Export CSV' is a plain text link with no feedback that it's the compliance path.
fixes: Label the proof line 'Signed by both sides' instead of 'committed frames'.
Make 'Export CSV' a labeled button with a 'for audit' suffix so Elena finds it instantly.
Add a 'Download proof' tooltip explaining what the hash proves.

top_issues: This file appears visually identical to 07-activity.png; if it is meant to be a dedicated detail view it adds no detail beyond the inline panel.
No route, time, or party expansion beyond what 07 already shows.
Proof is shown as a hash with no deeper audit trail (full frame path).
fixes: If a dedicated detail screen is intended, add the full route, exact timestamps, and the complete proof/frame path.
Otherwise remove the duplicate to avoid confusion in the review set.
Add an 'Audit view' that expands frame hashes and both signers.

top_issues: 'Risk color: Violet/Red/Orange' lets users choose a risk color, which makes color the only risk signal and invites a collision with the settled-green.
The 'At this scale' bar demo is clever but not obviously about exposure vs promises.
'Reveal recovery phrase' is a destructive-action plain button with no warning state.
fixes: Keep violet default and forbid a risk color that collides with settled-green.
Add a caption to the sample: 'Purple = promised. Green = yours now.'
Make 'Reveal recovery phrase' a two-tap confirm with a warning badge.

top_issues: The From/To cards are clear, but 'Reserve to account posts collateral on-chain' hides the on-chain fee and confirmation time.
'Fund you through H1' is a plausible but unexplained outcome in the What-happens panel.
'Add to batch' is unexplained for a first-time mover.
fixes: Add the expected on-chain fee and confirmation time to the 'What happens' panel for reserve moves.
Add an info note: 'This move uses the on-chain Depository, so it costs gas and takes one confirmation.'
Explain 'Add to batch' with a one-line tooltip (combine with other moves before signing).

top_issues: 'WHERE YOUR MONEY STANDS' is a great frame, but 'Promised by hubs $90.00' and 'You owe $0.00' reuse home colors with no inline legend.
The six nav tiles are good, but 'Lending' and 'Ownership' are unexplained until clicked.
'Needs attention: Nothing waiting on you' is reassuring but the empty state is visually large.
fixes: Add the color legend inline here, not only on Home.
Add a one-line subtitle under each tile (e.g., 'Lending — lend into a hub pool or borrow').
Compress the 'Needs attention' empty state to a single compact row.

top_issues: 'Depository may pull 0.00' is confusing phrasing for a balance line.
'Debts' is a big card that only explains itself in a buried paragraph when there is no debt.
Faucets are correctly labeled test-only, but the 'Prepare to receive / Available 25.50' repeats the receive-screen capacity jargon.
fixes: Change 'Depository may pull' to 'Available from Depository'.
Show the Debts card only when a debt exists; otherwise collapse it to a single line.
Replace 'Available 25.50' with 'This hub can accept 25.50 for you now.'

top_issues: '=100% per term' for 100 basis points is mathematically literate but confusing to non-analysts.
Lend/Borrow tabs and pool stats are clear, but 'Your offer sits in the hub pool until borrowed' leaves APY/annualization implicit.
'Active principal' in the pool panel is under-labeled.
fixes: Show '≈1.0% per 1-day term' and add 'APY depends on how often it renews'.
Add a clear 'What you earn if filled' line before the Offer button.
Rename 'Active principal' to 'Currently lent out'.

top_issues: 'A lazy entity is identified by the hash of its board' is opaque jargon.
The 'you' badge next to the signer is the clearest element but the threshold '1 of 1' is not stated as a risk.
'Take control of another entity' is an empty panel with no guidance.
fixes: Lead with 'This wallet is controlled by 1 of 1 keys — you. Losing this key loses the wallet.'
State the threshold as a plain risk line: 'Only your key can approve board changes.'
Add a short 'How to add a co-signer' link in the empty panel.

top_issues: 'Enforceable right now $40.00' is the strongest screen in the set — excellent separation of enforceable vs promised.
'Nothing in it isn't yours' is a double negative and weak closing copy.
'Violet is what a counterparty owes you on their signature alone, if they vanish, that is the most you can lose' is dense for a risk framing.
fixes: Replace the footer with 'Every amount listed here is yours and yours alone.'
Add 'could fail' next to the promised amount: 'Promised $90.00 — could fail if the hub vanishes.'
Add a per-counterparty 'reduce the promise' action that links directly to Move/Dispute.

top_issues: Account-lane table headers (PROMISED / YOU OWE / CREDIT OUT) are tiny and the money columns mix '+80.00' positions with '150.00/25.50' without consistent alignment.
The order book and account lanes are dense but highly legible for traders — a genuine strength.
No row hover/highlight, so scanning a specific hub lane is easy to lose.
fixes: Left-align all money columns and increase header size for readability.
Add row hover highlight and a click-to-open the hub account lane.
Add a keyboard shortcut hint for the palette in the footer.

top_issues: 'Jump to... (HK)' is cryptic — no visible hint that the palette exists for first-time users.
The palette is excellent for power users but invisible to non-keyboard users.
Items are well labeled with route hints (send money, book at the hub) which aids discovery.
fixes: Add a 'Press ⌘K' hint in the Desk footer and on Home.
Add a visible 'Search' button in the header as a mouse-friendly entry.
Keep the route hints — they are the best plain-language element in the review set.

overall.verdict: xln is a genuinely strong, protocol-true wallet: the sovereignty and account screens separate what is enforceable from what is promised better than most wallets, every agreement is co-signed and provable, and the desk and order book are excellent for traders. But it leaks arcane protocol jargon (frame, co-signed, prepare incoming account, credit room) into consumer-facing surfaces and leans on color-only meaning, which will lose the less-technical half of the ten users and dead-ends first-time cross-network swappers.
priority_fixes: Add a single plain-English line above the Home balance bar ('Green = yours now, purple = promised and could fail') and put text labels on the bar segments instead of color-only meaning — helps Rosa, Lucas, Jamal.
Add first-encounter tooltips or a plain-language mode for the words frame, co-signed, credit line, promised, and prepare incoming account across Pay/Receipt/Receive — helps Lucas, Rosa, Priya.
Make 'instantly spendable' a single prominent number on Home and replace 'receive up to X' phrasing — helps Jamal and Priya.
Fix the cross-network swap so the 'prepare incoming capacity' state offers a one-tap 'Add collateral now' step instead of dead-ending the flow — helps Aisha and Wei.
Replace 'committed frames' with 'signed by both sides' in Activity/Receipt and rename 'Prepare incoming account' to 'Choose where this payment lands' — helps Elena, Priya, and Noah.
